correctness.rationale: For each distinct pair of prism vertices the four distance types are 1/2/3 exactly as the original graph adjacency and horizontal two-step paths require. At scale one the clique complex is two copies of the join of discrete sets D_ai, each a bouquet of B spheres of dimension k−1, joined by N isolated matching bridges and hence N−1 additional circles. At scale two complete between-part adjacency makes the flag complex the join over i of Cl(K_ai square K2); each local two-simplex-and-ai-matchings complex is a bouquet of ai−1 circles. The join is a bouquet of B spheres of dimension 2k−1. Scale three is a simplex. Homology degrees at consecutive scales differ, giving all persistence intervals. Oriented matching-edge integer cycles have coefficient sum zero, identifying each integral local H1 as an augmentation lattice; part permutations act naturally and the layer swap acts by −1 on each factor, hence (−1)^k. This is an analytic all-k, all-ai proof, not an inference from finite tests.
residual_risks: Finite F2 tests cannot prove integral torsion-freeness, all sizes or equivariance; those rely on exact join/augmentation proof.
The quotient contraction of layer simplices need not itself be equivariant as chosen; induced symmetry is instead justified independently on the matching-edge cycle lattice.

value.rationale: Complete graph-metric Rips persistent homology and the integral equivariant top homology of a natural k-parameter family of Cartesian graph prisms is a motivated, reusable exact classification. It displays the nontrivial change from 2B top classes in degree k−1 at radius 1 to B in degree 2k−1 at radius 2, together with N−1 geometric circles, all integer torsion information and layer-swap parity. It is not merely the known cube table entry, nor an arbitrary numerical slice. The arguments use elementary joins once the difficult exact metric/flag decomposition is recognized; no broad Rips product theorem is asserted.
residual_risks: Restricts to finite unweighted vertex graph metric and complete multipartite first factor, not continuous edge realization or arbitrary graph Cartesian products.
The result is an explicit classification within a specialized but canonical graph class, not a general stability theorem.
